skill.name: pdf
skill.description: PDF manipulation toolkit for extracting text and tables, creating PDFs, merging and splitting documents, converting pages to images, and filling PDF forms.
skill.summary: Process, create, extract, merge, split, and fill PDF documents with guided examples and helper scripts.
skill.author: Cam10001110101

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command, network, and blocker findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks, comments, or reference links. Confirmed findings are expected local filesystem reads and writes plus a few documented shell utility examples. No prompt injection, exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Local file writes can overwrite user files.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit output paths, avoid writing over inputs, and use a dedicated working directory for generated PDFs and JSON files.

remediation.issue: Documented shell utilities run outside the Python process.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before running qpdf, pdftk, pdftotext, or pdfimages, especially on untrusted PDFs.
Validate output paths against a user-approved workspace and reject parent-directory traversal when possible.

remediation.issue: PDF parsing dependencies process complex untrusted files.
remediation.suggestion: Keep PDF libraries updated and prefer sandboxed execution for unknown or externally supplied documents.

content.value_statement: PDF workflows often need extraction, form filling, and document assembly across many files. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical PDF recipes and helper scripts.
actual_capabilities: Extract text, metadata, annotations, and tables from PDF documents.
Merge, split, rotate, crop, watermark, encrypt, and decrypt PDFs.
Convert PDF pages to images for visual review and OCR workflows.
Detect fillable form fields and generate field information files.
Fill PDF forms through native fields or text annotations.
Create new PDFs with Python and JavaScript library examples.
limitations: Requires local Python libraries or command-line tools before examples can run.
Does not guarantee accurate OCR for low-quality scanned documents.
Non-fillable form workflows need manual validation of bounding boxes.
Scripts write local output files and can overwrite paths chosen by the user.

use_cases.title: Fill Recurring Forms
use_cases.description: Prepare completed PDF forms by extracting field names, mapping values, and writing a finished document.

use_cases.title: Extract Document Data
use_cases.description: Pull text, tables, metadata, or annotations from PDFs for review, reporting, or migration work.

use_cases.title: Automate Document Assembly
use_cases.description: Merge, split, watermark, encrypt, or create PDFs as part of a repeatable document workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Text From a PDF
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PDF skill to extract readable text from this PDF. Tell me which method fits the document and save the output as a text file.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Simple PDF Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this PDF has fillable fields. Extract the field list, ask me for missing values, validate the entries, and create a filled PDF.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a PDF Packet
prompt_templates.prompt: Merge these PDFs in the order I provide, rotate any pages that need correction, and produce one final packet with clear output naming.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe batch workflow for a folder of PDFs. Extract text, preserve per-file outputs, log failures, and avoid overwriting source files.

output_examples.input: A user provides a benefits form PDF and the values to enter.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies fillable fields, maps each value, validates checkbox options, and creates a completed PDF for review.

output_examples.input: A user provides several PDFs that must become one packet.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists the chosen order, merges the files, checks page count, and saves a single combined document.

output_examples.input: A user needs tables from a monthly PDF report.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects a table extraction method, extracts the tables, and summarizes any pages that need manual review.

best_practices: Keep source PDFs and generated files in a dedicated working folder.
Inspect converted page images before writing annotations to a non-fillable form.
Verify final PDFs in a viewer after form filling, encryption, or page changes.
anti_patterns: Running command-line examples on untrusted PDFs without a sandbox.
Guessing form field locations without validation images.
Writing generated outputs over original documents.

faq.question: Can this skill fill PDF forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports fillable fields and annotation-based filling for PDFs without form fields.

faq.question: Can it extract tables?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes pdfplumber examples for extracting tables and converting them into structured data.

faq.question: Does it work with scanned PDFs?
faq.answer: It can guide OCR workflows, but OCR quality depends on scan clarity and installed OCR tools.

faq.question: Does it require local dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. Many workflows require Python packages or command-line PDF utilities installed locally.

faq.question: Can it modify existing PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for merging, splitting, rotating, cropping, watermarking, encrypting, and filling documents.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive PDFs?
faq.answer: Use a private working directory and avoid running external tools on untrusted files without isolation.
